Butter Unsalted 200g (Arla): Sweet cream butter made without salt. Clean, mild and faintly nutty — the dairy flavour comes through where salt would cover it.
Cheddar Burger Slices 130g (Emborg): Processed cheddar in burger-sized slices. Mild and salty, with a smooth elastic melt — built to melt evenly rather than to taste strongly.
Danish Blue Cheese 100g (Castello): A soft blue cheese veined through with mould. Creamy and crumbly at once, sharply salty with a metallic tang — one of the strongest things on the counter.
Emmenthaler (Emborg): A firm Swiss cheese with big holes through it, pale yellow and springy. Nutty and mildly sweet, mellow enough to eat in slices rather than in shavings.
Gran Amici (Emborg): A hard aged cheese in the Italian grating style. Dry, grainy and crystalline, salty and nutty — strong enough that a little covers a dish.
Grana Padano (Emborg): A hard Italian cheese aged until it turns grainy and crystalline. Salty and nutty, a touch gentler and less sharp than Parmigiano.
Grated Parmesan Cheese 226g (Euro Chef): Hard Italian cheese, already grated fine. Dry, sharp and very salty, with the concentrated savoury hit that long ageing gives.
Greek Yoghurt 500g (Naturalmind): Yoghurt strained until most of the whey is gone, which is what thickens it. Dense enough to stand a spoon in, clean and tart and rich in the mouth.
Homemade Yoghurt 500ml (Naturalmind): Unstrained yoghurt, made in small batches. Looser and lighter than the Greek one — mildly tart and fresh rather than rich.
Kefir Homemade: Milk fermented with kefir grains, which takes it further than yoghurt. Thin enough to drink, sharply sour, with a faint natural sparkle to it.
Mozzarella Cheese (Sausage Guy): Firm, low-moisture mozzarella, not the soft wet kind kept in brine. Mild and milky with a springy, squeaky bite, and it pulls into long strands when it melts.
Mozzarella in Brine 100g (Bayernland): Fresh mozzarella kept in brine, soft and wet right through. Very mild and milky with a light saltiness — a different cheese from the firm kind, not a softer version of it.
Premium Red Cheddar (Sausage Guy): Cheddar coloured deep orange, as red cheddar always is — the colour changes the look and not the taste. Firm and close-textured, sharp and savoury with a dry edge.
White Cheddar (Emborg): Cheddar left the pale colour it is naturally, instead of being dyed orange. Firm and savoury with a clean tang — the same cheddar bite, undyed.
Raw Milk 1L: Unpasteurised milk, sold frozen by the litre, from cow, carabao or goat. Carabao is the richest and creamiest; the goat milk has a distinct tang. Defrost it in the chiller and use within two to three days.
